- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–20% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (prices bouncing back after sharp drop), model should not overreact to new sentiment spikes.  
- After a spike in price (forecast > true), model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust next period’s forecast upward by 5–15% to counteract lag.  
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is trending down, avoid extreme lows — add 3–5% buffer to prevent premature bottoming.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model should not overfit to recent volatility — use 3–5 day smoothing to avoid false momentum.  
- If true outcome is consistently higher than forecast (especially after low sentiment), model may be underestimating demand — increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 periods.  
- If forecast is consistently lower than true outcome (especially after high sentiment), model may be underestimating sentiment impact — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 periods.
